title: The Man Who Beat the Wheel

lines.tts: In 1880, a broke cotton man beat a casino without cheating once.
lines.text: In 1880, a broke cotton man beat a casino without cheating once.

lines.tts: Joseph Jagger works in the mills of Yorkshire, watching spinning machines all day.
lines.text: Joseph Jagger works in the mills of Yorkshire, watching spinning machines all day.

lines.tts: Then his business fails. He's broke, with four kids to feed.
lines.text: Then his business fails. He's broke, with four kids to feed.

lines.tts: But all those years taught him one thing. Nothing that spins is ever perfectly balanced.
lines.text: But all those years taught him one thing. Nothing that spins is ever perfectly balanced.

lines.tts: So he borrows money, grabs his son and his nephew, and goes to Monte Carlo.
lines.text: So he borrows money, grabs his son and his nephew, and goes to Monte Carlo.

lines.tts: For a month, they don't bet a single coin. They just watch the roulette wheels, and write down every number.
lines.text: For a month, they don't bet a single coin. They just watch the roulette wheels, and write down every number.

lines.tts: And one wheel is lazy as hell. Some numbers come up way more than they should.

lines.tts: So Jagger starts betting on that wheel. And he wins. And wins. And wins.
lines.text: So Jagger starts betting on that wheel. And he wins. And wins. And wins.

lines.tts: Each table only holds a hundred thousand francs. He empties it, and the game stops until they bring more money.

lines.tts: You see, a roulette wheel is like a shopping cart with one bad wheel. You don't notice it, until you push it a thousand times.

lines.tts: In a few days, he's up over two million francs.

lines.tts: The casino panics, and the wheel makers add parts that move, so no wheel can stay lazy.

lines.tts: But it's too late. Jagger has already gone home.

lines.tts: Everyone knows the house always wins. So Jagger took the money, and bought houses.
